Source Function • Using the expressions for the emission/absorption coefficients j_ν = (hν/4π)φ(ν)n₂A₂₁, κ_ν = (hν/4π)φ(ν)(n₁B₁₂ − n₂B₂₁), one can write an expression for the source function S_ν = j_ν/κ_ν = n₂A₂₁/(n₁B₁₂ − n₂B₂₁) = (A₂₁/B₂₁)·1/(n₁B₁₂/n₂B₂₁ − 1) = (2hν³/c²)·1/((n₁/g₁)/(n₂/g₂) − 1)
• In LTE, S_ν becomes equal to the Planck function B_ν(T).
• In general, n₂/n₁ does not follow the Boltzmann equation. In this case, one can define the excitation temperature T_ex such that n₂/n₁ = (g₂/g₁)e^{−hν/kT_ex} – Then, S_ν = B_ν(T_ex).
Maser • The absorption coefficient can be written as κ_ν = n₁σ_ν = (hν/4π)φ(ν)n₁B₁₂(1 − (n₂/g₂)/(n₁/g₁))
• Usual situations, (n₂/g₂)/(n₁/g₁) = (n₂/n₁)(g₁/g₂) = exp(−E₁₂/kT_ex) < 1 ➔ κ_ν > 0

• If (n₂/g₂)/(n₁/g₁) > 1 (inverted populations), κ_ν < 0 – Results in radiation amplification: maser! (OH, H₂O, SiO, etc.) Microwave Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation [그림: 에너지 준위 — ground state에서 pumping으로 short-lived state로 올라감 → rapid decay로 metastable state에 많이(빨간 점 7개) 쌓임 → metastable→ground(점 2개) 전이로 Maser light]
Line Broadening • Doppler broadening – Due to Doppler shift of each atom/ion that is in thermal motion
• Natural broadening – Due to uncertainty principle, the energy levels occupied by an electron have finite width (spread).
• Collisional broadening – If the atom suffers collisions with other particles while it is emitting, the phase of the emitted radiation can be altered suddenly.
Doppler Broadening • The change in frequency associated with an atom with velocity component v along the line of sight is (ν − ν₀)/ν₀ = δν/ν₀ = −v/c (v > 0 when the atoms move away)
• Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution of gas f(v) = (m/2πkT)^{1/2} v² exp(−mv²/2kT)
note: 9/10 수업에서 교수님: 시선방향 1차원 분포이므로 v² 없어야 함 — 수정 예정

raw: • The associated line profile is φ(ν) = (1/(√π Δν_D)) e^{−(ν−ν₀)²/Δν_D²} where Δν_D = (ν₀/c)√(2kT/m) : Doppler line width
• Full width at half maximum (FWHM) Δν_FWHM = 2√(ln2) Δν_D [그림: ν₀(line center)에 피크 φ(ν₀)인 가우시안, φ(ν₀)/2 높이에 빨간 수평선 = FWHM]
Line Center Cross Section φ(ν) = (1/(√πΔν_D))e^{−(ν−ν₀)²/Δν_D²} • At the line center, the profile function becomes φ(ν₀) = 1/(√πΔν_D)

• The absorption cross-section at the line-center for each atom, neglecting the stimulated emission (in optical), is therefore κ_ν = n₁σ_ν = (hν/4π)(n₁B₁₂ − n₂B₂₁[빨간 사선으로 지움])φ(ν) ⟹ σ_ν0 = B₁₂(hν₀/4π)φ(ν₀) = (1/(√πΔν_D))(hν₀/4π)B₁₂ – σ_ν0 can be calculated observationally if B₁₂ is known.
Natural Broadening • The uncertainty principle implies that the spread in energy ΔE and the duration Δt in an energy level must satisfy ΔEΔt ∼ ℏ.

• According the classical theory, the resulting line profile is described the Lorenz profile: φ(ν) = (1/π)(γ/4π)/[(ν − ν₀)² + (γ/4π)²] – γ is the damping constant given by γ = Σ_{n″} A_{nn″} + Σ_{n″} A_{n′n″} – Its FWHM is Δν_L = γ/2π, Δλ_L = (λ₀/ν₀)Δν_L
• Example: For Hα 6563 Å lines, A₂₁ = 4.4×10⁷ s⁻¹ – Δν_L = 7.0×10⁶ Hz and Δλ_L = 1.0×10⁻⁴ Å. – cf. Δλ_FWHM = 0.35 Å due to Doppler effects in a cloud with T=10⁴ K
note: 계산: Δν_L=7.00×10⁶ Hz, Δλ_L=1.0×10⁻⁴ Å 일치. 도플러: 순수 수소 열운동 T=10⁴ K이면 Δλ_D=0.28 Å, FWHM=0.47 Å — PPT 0.35 Å와 차이

raw: Collisional Broadening • If an atom suffers collisions with other particles while it is emitting, the phase of the emitted radiation can be altered suddenly. • If the phase changes completely randomly at the collision times, then information about the emitting frequency is lost.

• If the collisions occur with frequency ν_col, that is, each atom experiences ν_col collisions per unit time on average, then the profile can be shown to follow φ(ν) = (1/π)(Γ/4π)/[(ν − ν₀)² + (Γ/4π)²] where Γ = γ + 2ν_col [그림: (a) 끊김 없는 사인파, (b) 시각 t₁, t₂에서 위상이 갑자기 바뀌는 사인파]
• Also called pressure broadening – Important when density is high.

Voigt Function • For real spectral lines, the Lorenz profile (due to natural/collisional broadening) must be convolved with the Gaussian distribution of particles φ(ν)^Voigt = ∫dv f(v) φ_L(ν − (v/c)ν₀) = (1/(√πΔν_D)) H(a,u) – f(v) : Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution – φ_L(ν): Lorenz profile

• Voigt function is defined as H(a,u) = (a/π)∫_{−∞}^{∞} e^{−y²}dy/(a² + (u − y)²), a = Γ/(4πΔν_D), u = (ν − ν₀)/Δν_D [그림: φ(ν)/Δν_FWHM vs Δν/Δν_FWHM — Gauss(실선, 중심 가장 높고 날개 빨리 떨어짐), Lorentz(점-쇄선, 날개 강함), Voigt(파선); 중앙 회색 띠가 Δν_FWHM]

HI 21 cm Lines • E₁₂ = 5.87 µeV; hν₁₂/k = 0.068 K – Since hν₁₂/kT ≪ 1, n₂/n₁ ~ g₂/g₁ = 3 under most situations. • A₂₁ = 3×10⁻¹⁵ s⁻¹ [그림: 수소 준위 n=1,2,3,∞; n=1 바닥 상태가 g₂=3(스핀 평행 ↑↑)과 g₁=1(반평행 ↑↓)로 갈라짐; λ₁₂ = 21 cm, ν₁₂ = 1.4 GHz]
note: 계산 E=5.874 µeV, hν/k=0.0682 K. 표준 A₂₁=2.87×10⁻¹⁵

raw: • The absorption coefficient for HI 21 lines κ_ν = (hν/4π)φ(ν)n₁B₁₂(1 − e^{−hν/kT}) = (hν/4π)φ(ν)·(1/4)n_H·(g₂/g₁)(c²/2hν³)A₂₁·(0.068/T) = 2.6×10⁻¹⁵ (n_H/T) φ(ν)
• Integrating κ_ν over the path length, τ_ν = ∫κ_ν dl = 2.6×10⁻¹⁵ (N_H/T) φ(ν) where N_H = ∫n_H dl : HI column density
HI Column Density • Integrating τ_ν over the frequency, N_H = 3.85×10¹⁴ T∫τ_ν dν (in cgs units)
• In radio astronomy, it is customary to express frequency in the velocity (km s⁻¹) using the Doppler relation dν = (ν/c)dv = dv/λ ➔ N_H = 1.82×10¹⁸ T∫τ_ν dv
• For emission lines, we use T_B = T(1 − e^{−τ_ν}) to obtain N_H = −1.82×10¹⁸ T∫ln(1 − T_B(v)/T) dv
– When optically thick, the above integral is undefined. Need to use absorption lines as well. – When optically thin, T_B = Tτ_ν and N_H/cm⁻² = 1.82×10¹⁸ ∫[T_B(v)/K] dv/(km s⁻¹)
